background.definition: Bronchiectasis is a condition of adults and children characterized by the permanent abnormal dilation of bronchi with the destruction of the elastic and muscular components of the bronchial walls, often due to acute or chronic infection. It may be focal or diffuse.

list.listitem: Among children, between 0.1 and 4 per 100,000 develop bronchiectasis annually.
About 3.3 per 100,000 children have bronchiectasis.
About 4% to 8% of adults referred for the evaluation of chronic productive cough have bronchiectasis.
About half of the patients with bronchiectasis have at least one underlying cause.
summarizes many of the causes of local and diffuse bronchiectasis.
Recurrent bacterial colonization and infection lead to progressive airway injury.
The injury activates inflammatory mediators, elastase, and collagenase with destruction of the elastic and muscular components of bronchial walls.
It is also associated with bronchial artery proliferation and arteriovenous malformations, predisposing patients to recurrent hemoptysis.
Encourage patients with bronchiectasis who smoke to quit. C
Vaccinate patients with bronchiectasis against influenza and pneumococcus. C
A UK study screened 1600 persons with bronchiectasis for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, and found only 8 persons with that condition (0.5%).

Suspect bronchiectasis in patients with a chronic daily cough productive of sputum who have been evaluated and treated for postnasal drip, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and asthma, and still have symptoms. C
The diagnosis is confirmed with a high-resolution CT scan. B
Perform a diagnostic evaluation for underlying disorders (see ) in patients without obvious underlying disease. B

Differential.Differential_Features: Dyspepsia, nocturnal symptoms, findings on endoscopy

list.listitem: Consider bronchiectasis in patients with a chronic daily cough productive of purulent sputum who have been evaluated and treated for postnasal drip, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and asthma, and still have symptoms.
Patients typically have chronic productive cough with excessive sputum volume, purulence, and tenacity.
Among adults with bronchiectasis, virtually all have chronic cough productive of sputum; however, only 30% have hemoptysis.
Among children with bronchiectasis, 75% have a chronic cough, 70% report sputum, 25% report hemoptysis, and about 50% wheeze and complain of dyspnea.
Evaluate patients for predisposing conditions such as COPD, asthma, gastroesophageal reflux, aspiration, inflammatory bowel disease, and rheumatologic conditions.
The physical examination may show rhonchi, crackles, and clubbing, but most often is normal.

Order CBC with differential and immunoglobulin levels (IgT, IgM, IgA and IgE) as part of the initial evaluation for immunodeficiency. Consider testing for cystic fibrosis, especially in younger patients.

CXR findings in patients with bronchiectasis include linear markings, bronchial wall thickening, patchy shadowing, loss of volume, and pleural thickening. Compared with bronchography, the sensitivity of CXR is about 13% to 40%, and the specificity is about 95%.
Radiologists reading CXRs in patients with bronchiectasis agree 70% of the time.
Because it is invasive, noxious, and risky, bronchography, long considered the gold standard, has been replaced by high-resolution CT.

Spirometry is not useful to establish the diagnosis of bronchiectasis; however, it is helpful in evaluating the presence of other underlying conditions, for identifying patients who might benefit from bronchodilators, and for monitoring purposes.

High-resolution CT scan is the gold standard for diagnosis. On high-resolution CT scan, there is enlarged internal bronchial diameter, with the bronchi appearing larger than the accompanying artery (the signet ring sign). In a study comparing conventional high-resolution CT with helical multidetector CT, the latter was more sensitive and specific for the detection of bronchiectasis.
During acute exacerbations, order sputum culture and sensitivity to guide therapy in patients who do not improve after initial empiric therapy.
In patients with a chronic productive cough, perform a workup for reflux, asthma, and postnasal drip (upper airway cough syndrome) first.
If no etiology is found and bronchiectasis is still suspected, make the diagnosis with a high-resolution CT.
Once the diagnosis of bronchiectasis is established, evaluate the patient for the underlying conditions summarized in .
In patients with exacerbations, use antibiotics that are active against Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas. B
Treat patients who have bronchiectasis with airflow obstruction or bronchial hyperreactivity using inhaled bronchodilators. B
In patients unable to expectorate effectively, use chest physiotherapy. B
Refer patients who have localized bronchiectasis unresponsive to medical therapy or associated with bronchial obstruction for bronchoscopy or surgery. B
Bronchodilators are commonly recommended for patients with airflow obstruction or bronchial hyperreactivity, but clinical trials in patients with bronchiectasis are lacking.

Brensocatib, an oral inhibitor of DPP-1, in doses of both 10 mg and 25 mg daily reduced pulmonary exacerbations over a one year period in a randomized trial with 1721 adults (1.03 vs 1.29 per year, p = 0.004).

Inhaled hyperosmolar agents such as mannitol increase mucus clearance, but long-term clinical data are lacking. A randomized trial of 40 patients found no difference in exacerbations or quality of life after 12 months between patients receiving inhaled 6% hypertonic saline and 0.9% isotonic saline.
A 2 x 2 factorial trial in 288 patients evaluated both carbocisteine and hypertonic saline as mucolytics. Neither was effective at reducing pulmonary exacerations over one year.
Mucolytics have not been shown to be beneficial in noncystic fibrosis bronchiectasis. rhDNase had increased adverse effects. Bromhexine may help with sputum production and clearance.

For prevention, long-term antibiotics reduce exacerbations and hospitalizations, but are also associated with adverse effects and may facilitate the emergence of resistant organisms. A single RCT of 141 adults with bronchiectasis not caused by cystic fibrosis found that daily azithromycin reduced exacerbations compared to placebo (NNT = 3 to prevent one exacerbation after 6 months) without increasing adverse effects. They should primarily be considered in patients with frequent (3 or more per year) exacerbations.
There is insufficient evidence to advise for or against inhaled NSAIDs in children or adults with bronchiectasis.

Inhaled steroids improve lung function in the short term, but long-term data addressing clinically relevant outcomes are limited. The only trial to evaluate long-term outcomes of inhaled steroids found no statistically significant improvements in any outcomes.
Inhaled antibiotics do not improve pulmonary function in noncystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, and adverse effects such as bronchospasm are more common, so do not use them.
There are no randomized trials about the use of systemic steroids, long-acting bronchodilators, anticholinergics, methylxanthines, or leukotriene receptor antagonists in bronchiectasis.
In patients with exacerbations, use systemic antibiotics for 2 weeks. The initial agents should be active against Haemophilus influenzae and Staphylococcus aureus.
Patients with cystic fibrosis or recent antibiotic use are at high risk for Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection; treat them accordingly.

In patients with inadequate response to initial treatment, use sputum culture and sensitivity results to guide the choice of either longer treatment with an oral agent or prolonged treatment with IV antibiotics.
Limit surgery to resect the bronchiectatic lung to patients with local disease who have severe symptoms and have not responded to medical therapy.
Patients with focal bronchiectasis due to bronchial obstruction are more likely to benefit from local interventions such as bronchoscopy or surgery than medications.
In patients with comorbid chronic rhinosinusitis and bronchiectasis, sinus surgery does not appear to reduce exacerbations.
Inspiratory muscle training improves endurance exercise capacity and health-related quality of life in the short term.
Other forms of physical training, including pulmonary rehabilitation have not been adequately studied in patients with bronchiectasis.

In patients who are unable to expectorate effectively, chest physiotherapy (chest percussion, vibration, postural drainage, mechanically assisted cough, airway oscillation) aids in clearing mucus. Positive expiratory pressure oscillators and high-frequency chest wall oscillation may also be helpful.
Based largely on expert opinion, one may recommend active cycle of breathing techniques, autogenic drainage, and slow exhalation with the glottis open in the lateral decubitus position.
Bronchiectasis is associated with chronic cough, multiple exacerbations, and progressive dyspnea that can become disabling. B
Disease progression is worse in patients with chronic colonization by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, severe exacerbations, and systemic inflammation. B

feature.caption: Conditions Associated with Bronchiectasis.
feature.feature_body:
Distribution Category Conditions
Focal Obstruction Foreign body, tumor, broncholithiasis, compression by peribronchial lymph nodes
Postinfectious Bacteria, tuberculosis, virus
Diffuse
Congenital/genetic Cystic fibrosis, primary ciliary dyskinesia, alpha1-antitrypsin deficiency, tracheobronchomegaly, cartilage deficiency, Marfan's syndrome
Chronic infection Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex, allergic bronchopulmonary mycoses (eg, Aspergillus)
Immunodeficiency Hypogammaglobulinemia, HIV
Toxic inhalation or aspiration Chlorine, gastroesophageal reflux disease
Rheumatic conditions Rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, Sjögren's syndrome, relapsing polychondritis
Miscellaneous Inflammatory bowel disease, Young's syndrome, pulmonary sequestration
Data from Rosen MJ. Chronic cough due to bronchiectasis: ACCP evidence-based clinical practice guidelines. Chest 2006 Jan;129(1 Suppl):122S–131S.
